Description: Identify 5-10 events that correlate with payment/retention. These are your 'growth events' — track them first before anything else.
Do_This: Map: signup → activation → aha moment → payment → retention|Start with 5 events max|Name consistently: object_action (e.g. project_created)|Include properties: plan_type, source, timestamp
Anti_Pattern: Tracking everything (100+ events with no strategy)|No naming convention|Frontend-only tracking (use backend for critical events)

Description: Create spreadsheet documenting every event before implementing. Columns: event_name, description, properties, trigger, priority.
Do_This: Columns: Event Name|Description|Properties|Trigger|Priority|Status|Use snake_case naming|Map events to business KPIs|Review weekly during sprints
Anti_Pattern: Starting implementation without tracking plan|Inconsistent names|No property documentation|Not mapping events to KPIs

Description: Install tracking SDK. PostHog: open-source, self-hostable, free tier 1M events. Mixpanel: cloud-hosted, free tier 20M events.
Do_This: PostHog: npm install posthog-js|Add to app init with project API key|Set up reverse proxy (prevents ad blockers)|Enable session replay|Configure autocapture for clicks
Anti_Pattern: No reverse proxy (ad blockers block 30%+ of data)|Using Google Analytics for product analytics|Multiple analytics tools with conflicting data

Description: Connect anonymous events to identified users after signup. Critical for funnel analysis and retention tracking.
Do_This: Call identify() on signup/login with user_id|Set user properties (plan, role, company)|Handle anonymous → identified merge|Don't identify with email (use internal ID)
Anti_Pattern: Not identifying users (all data is anonymous)|Using email as ID (privacy + change issues)|Multiple IDs per user (identity resolution mess)

Description: Create 3 core funnels: Signup → Activation, Activation → Payment, Payment → Retention. Find where users drop off.
Do_This: Signup → Onboarding Complete → Aha Moment → First Payment|Set conversion windows (7 days for activation)|Segment by source and plan|Review weekly|Act on biggest drop-off first
Anti_Pattern: Too many funnels (start with 3)|No conversion window|Not segmenting (averages hide insights)|Reviewing monthly instead of weekly

Description: Track retention by cohort: what % of users return in week 2, 4, 8, 12? Flattening retention curve = PMF signal.
Do_This: Create weekly retention table by signup cohort|Track: Day 1, Day 7, Day 30, Day 90 retention|Compare cohorts over time (improving = product improving)|Set up alerting if retention drops below threshold
Anti_Pattern: Only tracking DAU/MAU (not cohort retention)|Monthly granularity (too slow for early-stage)|Not comparing cohorts (can't see improvement)

Description: Track which features users actually use. Breadth (how many features) + Depth (how often per feature). Informs roadmap.
Do_This: Track feature_used event with feature_name property|Create feature adoption dashboard|Measure: % users who tried feature, % who use weekly|Identify underused features (improve discoverability or remove)|Link to NPS/satisfaction data
Anti_Pattern: Building features nobody uses (check data first)|Only tracking page views|No feature-level granularity|Not acting on low-adoption features

Description: Run A/B tests using feature flags. Test one variable at a time. Minimum sample: 1000 events per variant for statistical significance.
Do_This: Write hypothesis before test|One variable per test|Wait for statistical significance (don't peek)|Document results in experiment log|Successful tests → ship to 100%
Anti_Pattern: Peeking at results too early|Testing too many variables|No hypothesis (random testing)|Not documenting results
